C09.content_en:
Ways to find public datasets — and how the main options compare

You are writing an article or a book and want a number like "how the US population moved over ten years", but you do not know where a citable public dataset lives, and searching stalls. Enter a topic and this tool lists what Google Dataset Search returns: the dataset name, provider, last-updated date and link.

Method / toolPricing modelNotes
This tool (DataForSEO)Pay per request. About $0.002 for 20 results (measured)Name, provider, update date and URL in one table. Save as CSV. Tested with English keywords
Google Dataset Search (by hand)FreeThe same index on screen. It has filters (update time, format, usage rights) and suits opening and checking items one by one
Government open-data portals (for example, data.gov)See the official siteSee the official site for coverage and features
Kaggle DatasetsSee the official siteMany datasets for analysis and machine learning. Better for finding raw material to analyze than for finding a citable source

Checked in November 2026. Prices change — confirm on each vendor's official site before you buy.

Why use this tool

  • Take the search results away as a table. Name, provider, update date and link sit side by side, a good first pass before you compare candidates.
  • About $0.002 for 20 results. About 500 searches per $1, so you can try many topics.
  • A few seconds. We measured about 3.5 seconds for "population united states".
  • The update date is visible. It helps you avoid stale data (some rows are blank).
  • Save as CSV. Keep a list of source links for later.

When it is not the right fit

  • You want to see the data itself → the table shows only name, provider, update date and link. Check the numbers on the provider's page.
  • You want only official government statistics → a government portal is more focused. In our sample "population united states", the list mixed FRED, Statista, CEIC and other aggregators. The provider name is what the page reports about itself, so a name such as a government agency does not guarantee the real source.
  • You need the usage terms → the table does not show them. Read the terms on the linked page before you use anything.
  • Results for non-English keywords → we tested English only.

This tool does one thing: list where public datasets on a topic are published.

FAQ

May I put the data in my article or book as is?

Terms differ per dataset. This tool does not judge it. Check the usage terms and the citation style at the provider.

Why are some update dates or providers blank?

We show exactly what the API returned. In our test ("population united states", 20 results), 2 rows had no provider and 3 had no update date.

Why is there no country or language selector?

The API works from the keyword alone.

Can I choose the number of results?

It is fixed at 20. In an earlier test, 40 results cost about $0.004 (measured).

Can I sign up with a free email address?

No. DataForSEO does not accept free email providers. See What is DataForSEO?

C10.content_en:
Ways to check which advertisers run Google Ads — and how the main tools compare

Is a rival shop or company running Google Ads or not? You can hardly ask them. Enter a company or shop name and this tool lists the advertisers Google has registered under that name: advertiser name, advertiser ID, country and an approximate ad count.

Method / toolPricing modelNotes
This tool (DataForSEO)Pay per request. About $0.002 (measured)Enter a company name; get advertiser name, ID, country and approximate ad count in a table. Save as CSV
Google Ads Transparency Center (by hand)FreeGoogle's own tool. Search by advertiser or website name and filter by region and date (per Google's help). You can see the ads themselves
Semrush Advertising ToolkitSubscription (Base and Pro plans; see the official site for prices)Researches competitors across ad channels. Broad, but large for a small shop
Ahrefs Site ExplorerSubscription (see the official site for plans)Has a paid-search view per site. Built for site analysis, not for listing advertisers

Checked in November 2026. Prices change — confirm on each vendor's official site before you buy.

Why use this tool

  • Look up by shop name. Even a short brand name like "nike" returned 7 advertiser rows in our sample, including look-alike names such as Nike Klara and Nikel Kola.
  • An ad-count estimate. A rough sense of how seriously an advertiser spends.
  • About $0.002 and a few seconds. Our "nike" lookup took about 0.6 seconds. About 500 lookups per $1, so you can check several rivals in a row.
  • Pick a country. Choose the US or another market (you cannot narrow to a city or area).
  • Save as CSV. Advertiser IDs come along.

When it is not the right fit

  • You want to search by domain → this tool looks up a name. Google also returns domain-name matches (10 of the 17 rows in our "nike" sample), but they carry no advertiser ID or ad count, so the table leaves them out.
  • You want to see the ads → the table has advertiser info only. Use the "see running ads" tool or Google's Transparency Center.
  • You need an exact ad count → the number is the API's approximate value.
  • A large company may show many advertiser IDs in one row (in our sample, "Nike, Inc." was one row listing two advertiser IDs, about 10,003 ads in total).

This tool does one thing: list the advertisers registered with Google under a name.

FAQ

What if the shop does not run ads?

You will see "No results found". That does not prove they run no ads; try another spelling.

Is the ad count the number of ads running now?

It is the API's approximate figure, shown as is. This tool cannot say whether it is current.

What is the advertiser ID for?

It is a key for finding that advertiser's ads in Google's Transparency Center.

Why does one company show several advertiser IDs?

Large companies can hold several advertiser accounts. In our "nike" lookup, the "Nike, Inc." row listed two IDs.

Can I sign up with a free email address?

No. DataForSEO does not accept free email providers. See What is DataForSEO?
